example_locator: src/clock.py (infer_offset_seconds); cross-source join of raw_auth login_success and raw_endpoint on host, against clean.db
root_cause: Endpoint clock offset investigated via cross-source anchor matching (auth login_success <-> endpoint event, joined on host, closest pair by time delta). Across 495 hosts with a matched pair, the median absolute delta was 11 seconds and no host's closest match fell anywhere near +/-3900 seconds - indicating no significant clock skew in the supplied archive, contrary to the schema fixture's example offset of -3900s, which represents the normalizer's capability to correct an offset (see src/clock.py apply_offset/infer_offset_seconds), not a confirmed property of this dataset.
detection_method: SQL join in DuckDB: auth login_success events joined to endpoint events on host, ranked by ABS(datediff('second', ep_time, auth_time)), single closest pair kept per host; distribution of resulting deltas examined (min/25%/median/75%/max, and explicit count near +/-3900s)
resolution_disposition: no offset applied to endpoint timestamps; decision is evidence-based, not a default/guess, and is reproducible via the SQL join described above

root_cause: The same real-world identity (amina-ad4, per identity-directory.csv) appears under two different raw string forms in two different sources: 'amina-ad4@example.invalid' in the auth login event, and 'EXAMPLE\amina-ad4' in the endpoint PowerShell-execution event. Without alias resolution, these would appear to be two unrelated identities, breaking the identity link that campaign 3 (password spray -> encoded PowerShell) depends on to attribute both events to the same actor. Confirmed by direct grep against both real uploaded files - each alias form appears in exactly one source and nowhere else.
detection_method: grep for each literal alias string against all 5 real source files; cross-referenced against identity-directory.csv's identity_id/canonical_name/alias mapping (id-v1-amina-ad4 -> amina-ad4, with both alias strings listed)
resolution_disposition: src/identity.py (canonicalize_identity) was not available in this chat to independently test the resolution function itself; this entry documents that the underlying data genuinely requires alias resolution to hold together, and that identity-directory.csv is the authoritative source for the mapping. If canonicalize_identity is not confirmed to resolve both forms to id-v1-amina-ad4, campaign 3's identity-attribution claim is at risk and should be re-verified against the actual identity.py before submission.

resolution_disposition: 0 genuine duplicate events confirmed across all 5 sources; no action needed beyond documenting the quarantine-row false-positive so a future duplicate check isn't mis-scoped the same way
